LPM.Title: Lockpick Minigames
LPM.Hint.sweetspot: Move the pick around the whole dial to find the sweet spot, then hold the left mouse button to turn the lock.
LPM.Hint.tumbler: The pins bind in a hidden order. Push a pin: only the binding pin pauses at its notch; click it during the pause to set it. Two test pushes per round are free, later ones cost pick health.
LPM.Hint.skillcheck: Click or press SPACE when the needle is inside the highlighted arc. The blue caps count double.
LPM.Hint.tension: Click the dial to start. Hold SPACE, the right mouse button, or the left button on the gauge to build tension.
LPM.Hint.tensionGo: Keep the marker inside the green band and left-click the glowing target.
LPM.Hint.trace: Click the S marker to start, then guide the cursor along the keyway to E without touching the walls.
LPM.Hint.traceGo: Steady… follow the keyway to the E marker.
LPM.Hint.traceHit: You scraped the ward. Click S to start again.

LPM.Setting.doorsDefault.Hint: Every locked door can be picked with the world defaults unless its own lock settings say otherwise. Tokens must always be configured.
LPM.Setting.defaultGame.Name: Default minigame

LPM.Setting.defaultTier.Name: Default difficulty
LPM.Setting.defaultTier.Hint: Used by locks that do not set their own tier.
LPM.Setting.interactionDistance.Name: Interaction distance
LPM.Setting.interactionDistance.Hint: Maximum distance in scene units from the player's token to the lock. 0 disables the check.
LPM.Setting.maxAttempts.Name: Default max attempts per player
LPM.Setting.maxAttempts.Hint: 0 is unlimited. Locks can override this.
LPM.Setting.jam.Name: Jam the lock when attempts run out
LPM.Setting.jam.Hint: A jammed lock refuses further picking until the GM resets it or a key is used.
LPM.Setting.cooldown.Name: Default cooldown after failure (seconds)
LPM.Setting.cooldown.Hint: 0 is none. Locks can override this.
LPM.Setting.skillPath.Name: Skill attribute path
LPM.Setting.skillPath.Hint: Used when the dnd5e formula is off or on other systems: actor data path of the number that lowers the difficulty, e.g. system.skills.slt.total or system.abilities.dex.mod. Leave empty for none.
LPM.Setting.skillDivisor.Name: Skill divisor
LPM.Setting.skillDivisor.Hint: The tier drops by floor(skill points / divisor). On dnd5e the points are Sleight of Hand + thieves' tools proficiency (doubled with both).
LPM.Setting.tools.Name: Lock-picking tools
LPM.Setting.tools.Hint: Item names with their amount, separated by semicolons: Thieves' Tools=2; Masterwork Picks=4. The best tool carried counts. On dnd5e the amount joins the skill points (so an unproficient character with tools still gets it); elsewhere it lowers the tier directly.
LPM.Setting.requireTool.Name: Tools required
LPM.Setting.requireTool.Hint: Players without one of the tools above cannot attempt a lock.
LPM.Setting.toolBreakChance.Name: Tool break chance on failure (%)
LPM.Setting.toolBreakChance.Hint: Chance that one of the tool items is consumed when an attempt fails.
LPM.Setting.openOnSuccess.Name: Open doors on success
LPM.Setting.openOnSuccess.Hint: Off: a picked door becomes unlocked and the player opens it with a second click.
LPM.Setting.chat.Name: Chat messages
LPM.Setting.chat.Hint: Whisper the outcome of every attempt to the GM and the player.

LPM.HowTo.Label: How to:
LPM.HowTo.sweetspot: Move the mouse around the dial; the pick follows it through a full circle, and somewhere on that circle is the sweet spot. Hold the left mouse button to turn the cylinder. On the spot it turns all the way and the lock opens (only tiers 1 and 2 also show a faint glow there). If it stops part-way, release at once: the pick shakes, turns red and loses health as long as you keep pushing. How far it turned tells you how close you are. One pick only. From tier 7 the mechanism settles after every strained push, so the sweet spot shifts slightly and you cannot bisect it forever.
LPM.HowTo.dual: Two phases. First, sweep the cursor over the dial: a blue glow around the cursor grows brighter the closer you are to the hidden spot. Hold still on it for a moment until a ring closes on it. Second, the spot (blue ring, white core) starts to wander. Hold SPACE or the left mouse button and keep the cursor on it: the rotation bar fills while you are on it, and the pick loses health while you hold off it. Release to stop the damage; rotation unwinds slowly while released. From tier 9 the spot blinks out for a moment now and then: keep following where it was heading.
LPM.HowTo.tumbler: The pins bind in a hidden random order that changes with every attempt. Click a column to push its pin up. Only the pin that currently binds pauses at its notch; every other pin springs straight back down, and pins you have tested this round turn dull. Click the binding pin during its pause to set it; set pins turn gold and stay at their notch, and the order moves on to the next pin. Two test pushes per round are free, every further push in the same round costs pick health, so remember which pins sprang back. Up to tier 9, a wrong push makes the binding pin's base glow for a moment (on the lowest tiers it glows all the time); above that you must find it yourself. Clicking while a pin is rising or falling is an error: it costs health and, from tier 6, drops the last set pin; from tier 11 it drops every set pin. Each pin has its own rise speed and pause length that re-roll every round; higher tiers add pins, shorten the pause and add fake pauses at the wrong height.
LPM.HowTo.skillcheck: A needle sweeps around the ring. Click or press SPACE the moment it is inside the highlighted arc. The yellow body counts one hit, the thin blue caps at either end count two. Every miss damages the pick, and a miss inside the red trap arc costs half again as much. After each hit the arc and the trap jump elsewhere, the needle may change speed or direction, and both arcs drift against the needle. From tier 8 the needle breathes, speeding up and slowing down. Reach the hit count shown at the top.
LPM.HowTo.tension: Click the dial to start. Tension builds while you hold SPACE, the right mouse button, or the left button on the gauge; it falls when you release. Keep the marker inside the green band, which drifts up and down and, from tier 7, breathes wider and narrower. While the marker is in the band, left-click the glowing target on the dial; clicking it outside the band is a miss. Targets expire (the ring around them counts down) and reappear elsewhere. From tier 10 the pick slips now and then (the gauge flashes red) and tension drops suddenly. Letting the marker reach the red cap burns the pick.
LPM.HowTo.trace: Click the green S marker, then move the cursor along the dark keyway to the yellow E marker without touching the walls. A touch damages the pick and sends you back to S. Every attempt draws a different keyway: zigzags, waves, stairs, switchbacks, hairpins, orbits, petals, spirals, grid walks and grid mazes. In a maze every corridor is safe to enter, but only the true route fills the progress bar, so dead ends cost time. Higher tiers are narrower and longer, from tier 7 the keyway is only visible near your cursor, and from tier 9 the walls breathe and a timer at the top runs while you trace: run out and the wards reset.
LPM.Setting.dndFormula.Name: dnd5e skill formula
LPM.Setting.dndFormula.Hint: Points = Sleight of Hand total + thieves' tools proficiency bonus + the flat amount of the best carried tool from the tools list; doubled when proficient in both the skill and the tools; the tier drops by floor(points / divisor). Off: use the skill attribute path below, with carried tools as a separate reduction.
LPM.Hint.sweetSettled: The mechanism settled; the sweet spot shifted a little.
